timeline_events.title: Occupational Health Assessment: HIGH Risk (Construction Site Mason (Tile & Silica Cutting))
timeline_events.details: Evaluated 6 years of worksite exposure. High hazard flags: Respirable Crystalline Silica (RCS) Dust (< 4 µm), Portland Cement Alkaline Hexavalent Chromium. Recommended: Chest X-Ray & Spirometry.

metadata.clinicalSummary: HIGH occupational hazard for Construction Masonry with 6 years of exposure. Recommended surveillance: Immediate (Within 1-2 Weeks) with Chest X-Ray & Spirometry.

predictedOccupationalConditions.description: Nodular pulmonary fibrosis caused by chronic inhalation of fine crystalline silica dust during brick cutting and plastering.

predictedOccupationalConditions.condition: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD / Industrial Bronchitis)
predictedOccupationalConditions.description: Progressive airflow obstruction and chronic productive cough from high-density cement particulates.
Deep epidermal fissures, hyperkeratosis, and ulceration from wet alkaline mortar and chromate salts.
Chronic mechanical lower back and knee degeneration from lifting heavy sand/brick sacks.

recommendedScreenings: High-Resolution Digital Chest X-Ray (ILO 2011/2022 Pneumoconiosis Standard)
Spirometry / Pulmonary Function Test (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC ratio)
Dermatological Patch Testing for Potassium Dichromate hypersensitivity
preventiveCareGuidance: Mandatory usage of certified N95 or FFP3 dust respirators (simple cloth masks fail against respirable silica).
Implement wet-cutting and dust suppression methods for all concrete block and tile cutting.
Wear heavy-duty nitrile-coated gloves with inner cotton liners and apply barrier creams before mixing cement.
Strict adherence to ergonomic two-person lifting protocols for loads exceeding 25 kg.
Mandatory 4-liter scheduled daily electrolyte hydration to prevent acute heat exhaustion and kidney strain.
metadata.clinicalFollowupInterval: Immediate (Within 1-2 Weeks) with Chest X-Ray & Spirometry
